The '''Theed Funeral Temple''' was a small [[temple]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] reserved for the traditional [[Cremation/Legends|cremations]] of the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]].

==History==
Constructed on the outskirts of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], the Funeral Temple was a quiet, reflective place sought out while mourning the [[Death/Legends|dead]]. An ancient domed building, the small [[temple]] had an open ceiling directly over the pyre at the interior chamber's center. It was at the temple that the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] dead were [[Cremation/Legends|cremated]], their lives celebrated by mourners who gathered in a tiered circle around the pyre.<ref name="TPM" />

It was [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] belief that a body had to be cremated within two [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of death in order to return the life force of the dead to the planet. Following the cremation, it was tradition for those closest to the deceased to throw the ashes from the short [[bridge]] between the temple and the [[Livet Tower/Legends|Livet Tower]], and into the [[Solleu River/Legends|Solleu River]] before its plunge over the cliff. The [[Eternal Flame]] within the Livet Tower served to remind the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] of the transience of their current life and their duty to lead harmonious lives.<ref name="IWSWE">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref>

[[File:Theed_pyre.png|thumb|left|250px|The pyre in the Funeral Temple, where Qui-Gon Jinn was cremated]]
Throughout the temple's history, many notable individuals were mourned at the temple. Following the deaths of his family, [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Vidar Kim]] wept openly as he carried the ashes of his [[Vidar Kim's wife|wife]] and [[Vidar Kim's first son|two]] [[Vidar Kim's second son|sons]] to be spread in the Solleu River.<ref name="Darth Plagueis novel">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> [[52 BBY/Legends|Two years]] later, Senator Kim was murdered by a [[Maladian]] [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] and was cremated in the [[Naboo Embassy]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], a small [[Candle/Legends|candle]] resting on his chest representing the Livet Tower's Eternal Flame.<ref name="Republic 64">[[Republic 64|''Republic'' 64]]</ref>

In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], following the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|unsuccessful invasion]] of the planet, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] was [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|cremated]] in the temple after his death at the hands of a [[Darth Maul/Legends|mysterious]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].<ref name="TPM" /> [[19 BBY/Legends|Over a decade]] later, at the close of the bloody [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], former [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] and [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] of Naboo [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] was, against the rules of the Naboo,<ref name="SWCL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> not cremated in the temple. Instead, her body was placed in a [[Tomb of Padmé Amidala/Legends|mausoleum]] under unknown circumstances.<ref name="Galaxy 7">{{Topps|set=2012 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 7|cardname=Mourning for Padmé}}</ref>
